note: Puphpeteer is a pdf_api submodule adding a 'puphpeteer' PdfGenerator backend that renders HTML to PDF with headless Chrome/Puppeteer (NigelCunningham\Puphpeteer\Puppeteer). It is intentionally NOT enabled in this environment (needs Node.js + the Puppeteer library / Chromium). Its behaviour is driven by the config object puphpeteer.settings (route puphpeteer.config at /admin/config/system/pdf-api/puphpeteer). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config object and its documented keys/defaults (executable_path='' , service=false, service_url='', pagedjs=false). Because the config object is not installed by default (module disabled), setup/reset scripts create it and cleanup DELETES it to restore the disabled baseline. No PDF is actually generated, so Node is not required to run these cases.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal pdf_api ecosystem, what does the puphpeteer submodule add, and what external runtime does it require to actually generate a PDF?
evals.expected_output: It registers a 'puphpeteer' PdfGenerator backend for pdf_api that renders HTML with a real headless Chrome browser driven by Puppeteer, giving full CSS/JS fidelity. It requires a Node.js runtime plus the Puppeteer library (NigelCunningham/puphpeteer, which installs Chromium).

evals.prompt: How do I configure the Drupal puphpeteer backend to connect to an already-running (external) Chrome/Puppeteer instance instead of launching its own? Name the config object and the keys involved.
evals.expected_output: In the puphpeteer.settings config object set service to true and service_url to the browserURL to connect to (used by puppeteer.connect). Editable at /admin/config/system/pdf-api/puphpeteer.

evals.prompt: Which puphpeteer setting makes it load paged.js for print-oriented pagination, and where is the puphpeteer settings form?
evals.expected_output: Enable the pagedjs boolean in puphpeteer.settings. The settings form is route puphpeteer.config at /admin/config/system/pdf-api/puphpeteer.

evals.prompt: On this site, the puphpeteer backend has been configured to use an external Puppeteer service. Inspect the live puphpeteer configuration and report the service URL it will connect to.
evals.expected_output: In puphpeteer.settings, service is true and service_url is http://chrome:9222. Read with: drush cget puphpeteer.settings service_url.

evals.prompt: Someone has been debugging the puphpeteer PDF backend on this site. Inspect the live puphpeteer configuration and state whether Chrome is currently set to run in headless mode.
evals.expected_output: No — in puphpeteer.settings the headless key is false (default is true). Read with: drush cget puphpeteer.settings headless.

evals.prompt: The puphpeteer backend on this site needs to know where Node lives. Configure its executable path to /usr/bin/node in the puphpeteer configuration and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In the puphpeteer.settings config object set executable_path to /usr/bin/node (e.g. drush cset -y puphpeteer.settings executable_path /usr/bin/node).

evals.prompt: Configure the puphpeteer PDF backend on this site to load paged.js so print-oriented pagination is applied. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: In the puphpeteer.settings config object set pagedjs to true (e.g. drush cset -y puphpeteer.settings pagedjs 1). The default is false.
